headline: Recommended requiring on-site inclusionary units for large projects, kept $80,000 payment-in-lieu fee with automatic adjustments, and lowered mixed-tenure threshold to 75 units.
summary: The joint Planning Commission and City Council Ordinance Committee working group reviewed inclusionary zoning (IZ) Proposals 3 through 7. The group favored requiring on-site IZ units for large projects, agreed to keep the $80,000 payment-in-lieu base fee with automatic yearly adjustments, and lowered the threshold for mixed-tenure IZ units from 200 to 75 units. No consensus was reached on Proposal 7 regarding home ownership opportunities at 100% AMI, and staff was told to keep studying it. Two public forums were held where residents commented on IZ thresholds, fees, and homeownership opportunities.
decisions: The group favored requiring all inclusionary zoning units to be built on-site for large projects, especially those over 75 units, rather than allowing off-site options.
The group agreed to keep the $80,000 base payment-in-lieu fee with automatic yearly adjustments based on construction cost indices, instead of requiring annual City Council approval.
The group lowered the unit threshold for allowing mixed rental and owner-occupied inclusionary zoning units from 200 units to 75 units.

1. Agenda
Call to Order: 6:02pm
Changes to Agenda: Agenda adopted by both City Council Ord. Committee & Planning
Commission
2. Director’s Report
C. Dillard shared updates on Tier 1A Application Work Session at City Council and also shared
that the Mayor will be hosting a press conference on Wednesday, Sept. 23, related to the housing
strategy.
3. Public Forum #1
Sharon Bushor: Shared that some members of the public may want their concerns to be
considered by the Working Group. Understands rationale for two public forums, but feels
comments have less value if shared at the end.
4. Follow-up presentation & discussion on Proposals 3, 4, and 5
Large Project Threshold for Proposals 3 & 4: Staff presented four options for regulating large
projects (75+ units or 3+ acres) regarding off-site and payment-in-lieu options, with option 4
(requiring on-site IZ units for projects with 75+ units or 3+ acres) being recommended. The
working group discussed the approach and discussed whether larger projects (200+) should be
allowed to place some IZ off-site rather than requiring all units to be on-site. While some members
supported more flexibility for larger projects (200+) to reduce complexity and facilitate
partnerships, the full group favored maintaining simplicity and requiring all IZ to be on-site,
particularly for projects over 75 units.
Burlington Planning Commission Minutes p. 2 
  
   
 
Payment-In-Lieu Reconfiguration (Proposal 5): The group discussed adjusting payment-in-lieu 
fees for affordable housing units, with Nancy presenting analysis showing current fees would 
trend to $100,000-$113,000 using different inflation measures. The team agreed to maintain the 
$80,000 base fee with automatic annual adjustments based on construction cost indices rather 
than requiring annual City Council approval. M. Gaughan suggested the use of a 12-month rolling 
average to smooth construction cost indices, highlighting the volatility in recent years, which the 
Working Group direct staff to include in the formula.  
5. Presentation & Discussion: Proposal 6 – Allow Tenure Flexibility in Large 
Projects 
Staff presented the proposal to allow tenure flexibility in large projects (over 200 units) by 
enabling IZ units to be either rental or owner-occupied, with a requirement that 20% of required IZ 
units be owner-occupied in projects including market rate owner-occupied units. Some members 
of the working group questioned why the flexibility was limited to large projects. The group agreed 
to lower the threshold from 200 units to 75 units for mixed tenure projects. The conversation also 
touched on the rarity of affordable homeownership projects and the challenges of creating 
conventional affordable condos. 
6. Presentation & Discussion: Proposal 7 – Home Ownership Opportunities at 
100% AMI 
Staff shared that, after feedback received from CHT, they recommend retracting this proposal and 
retain existing language. Instead, non-IZ tools should be leveraged to produce middle-income 
ownership units.  
• Michael from Champlain Housing Trust explained their shared equity program, clarifying that 
while units are priced at 70% of AMI, they can be sold to buyers up to 100% of median 
income, and emphasized the importance of permanently affordable housing through shared 
equity mechanisms. Highlighted the balance between affordability and wealth-building 
through home ownership, with Michael explaining how their program helps families build 
equity while remaining affordable to future generations. 
• There was not a consensus on whether or not the initial proposal should be retracted, 
pursued, or whether a compromise should be explored. Staff was directed to continue 
exploring the options based on the discussion.  
• S. Carpenter requested that staff explores what is meant by “permanent affordability”.  
7. Public Forum #2 
Jak Tiano: Representing Let’s Build Homes, emphasized that unfunded IZ requirements can 
increase housing costs or make projects financially infeasible, particularly for small - 
and mid-sized developments with limited access to outside funding. Noted that larger 
projects may be better positioned to leverage public funding and affordable housing 
partnerships, and encouraged the Working Group to use a data-driven approach to 
identify project thresholds where these funding opportunities become available.  
Sharon 
Bushor: 
Sharon supported requiring on-site IZ for projects with 75+ units or 3+ acres, while 
raising concerns about neighborhood gentrification, the payment-in-lieu fee, support 
for smaller developers, and ensuring adequate affordable homeownership 
opportunities. She recommended providing educational resources on AMI and IZ to 
help the public offer more informed feedback. 
8. Accept Communications 
9. Adjournment (9:00pm) 
Action: Joint motion to adjourn 
Motion by: A. Montroll Seconded by: n/a Vote: Unanimous
